title: Mortadella Farfalle Antipasto Tray
seoTitle: Mortadella Farfalle Antipasto Tray | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Antipasto pasta salad—grilled veg, cured meat, hall tray that holds cold
subtitle: Grilled veg, salami, pepperoncini, and Italian dressing for ten
description: Rotini tosses with grilled zucchini and peppers, Genoa salami, pepperoncini, provolone, and zesty Italian dressing. A big antipasto-inspired tray for ten.

steps.title: Boil pasta
steps.instruction: Cook rotini in salted water to al dente. Drain, rinse cold, and toss with a little oil. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prep veg for grill
steps.instruction: Toss zucchini, peppers, and onion chunks with oil, salt, and pepper. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F with a 3-minute rest on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill vegetables
steps.instruction: Grill veg in basket at 400°F until charred and tender, 10–12 minutes. Cool and chop. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build dressing
steps.instruction: Whisk olive oil, vinegar, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Assemble antipasto salad
steps.instruction: Toss pasta with dressing, grilled veg, salami, pepperoncini, and provolone. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F with a 3-minute rest on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Chill before service
steps.instruction: Chill at least 30 minutes so flavors meld. Hold refrigerated up to 48 hours. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tray for ten
steps.instruction: Spread in a hotel pan. Top with extra pepperoncini and provolone at the line. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Call guidance
steps.instruction: Antipasto pasta salad is call-proof—make ahead and pull from cooler anytime. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Rinse pasta cold to stop cooking and keep salad from gumming.
Pepperoncini brine in dressing adds antipasto punch—save a splash.
Salami is the salt—taste before adding extra dressing salt.
tonightSpread: Cold side that balances hot grill mains.
leftovers: Bake into a cheesy pasta frittata.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Antipasto flavors in pasta salad form beat plain macaroni salad. Grilled veg adds smoke; pepperoncini adds punch. Tray holds refrigerated all shift.
mealPrepNotes: Grill veg at 400°F while pasta boils. Chill salad at least 30 minutes before service. Holds refrigerated 48 hours—pull from cooler before plating.
